findings.title: approval_foreign_decision is claimed as tested but no assertion depends on it
findings.location: src/factory/releases.ts:1018 (guard); tasks/factory/w07b-GATES.md G2 EXPECT (claim); src/__tests__/helpers/factory-release-suite.ts:907-908 (the test sequence that gestures at it without asserting it)
findings.evidence: Mutation test 'remove-approval_foreign_decision-guard' above: 24 pass / 0 fail with the guard deleted.
findings.detail: factory-release-suite.ts:899-908 moves an approval's operation_id onto a foreign operation, asserts the operation_id-binding effect (kind becomes 'policy'), then sets decision_id back to the suite's single shared decisionId and asserts the approval now serves. Because every operation in this suite is built from the same shared decisionId (factory-release-suite.ts:26, :130), decision_id already matched before that UPDATE ran, so the UPDATE is a no-op and the preceding comment ('it still cannot serve, because its decision no longer matches') describes a state the test never actually produces or checks. No case in the suite ever sets decision_id to a value that genuinely differs from the operation's own decisionId while operation_id, expected_generation, and status are otherwise valid.
findings.required_fix: Either (a) add a genuine case: create a second accepted decision (a second assurance.accept()) or directly corrupt decision_id to an unrelated string on a row that is otherwise fully valid, and assert { kind: 'none', reason: 'approval_foreign_decision' }; or (b) if the team judges this guard truly unreachable through any application code path (assurance.ts only ever writes decision_id equal to the operation's own decisionId at creation), say so plainly in the gate file instead of claiming it is 'reachable through the decision check', matching the honesty already applied to 'approval_foreign_decision... only a direct row edit produces it' in the Open section.
findings.security_impact: None found. The primary binding claim in decision #1 ('never a consent from another run, candidate, or node') is independently satisfied by the operation_id predicate in the SELECT's WHERE clause, which digests projectId/runId/nodeInstanceId/candidateGeneration/candidateDigest/action/destination (releases.ts:380-382). decision_id is a second, narrower check on top of an already-matched row, not the thing that prevents cross-run/cross-node/cross-candidate reuse.

findings.title: A structurally related, equally untested disjunct exists one line below F1
findings.location: src/factory/releases.ts:1019 — the `current.approved_grant_revision === null` arm of the approval_not_approved check
findings.evidence: src/factory/assurance.ts:239 always writes approved_by and approved_grant_revision in the same UPDATE statement, so the application never produces a row with one set and the other null; only a direct row edit could. This specific disjunct is not tested by any case that isolates it (the two approval_not_approved cases in the suite null out approved_by, not approved_grant_revision).
findings.required_fix: Optional. Same class of issue as F1 (defense against direct data corruption, not an application-reachable state). No action required unless F1 is fixed by adding corruption-style tests, in which case add the matching one for symmetry.
